Cleaner strokes. Balanced geometry.

A closer review of the same 977 icons. Weak contours were reconstructed in their existing source files, with the original names and source IDs preserved. Compare the earlier drawing with the rebuilt result below.

A stroke is one continuous drawn path; segments are the lines and curves that form it. Use either count to sort. Blue shows each centerline. Nodes include every internal cubic knot. Enable Curve handles to inspect the direction and continuity inside each stroke. Turn Centerlines off to judge the full stroke. Reconstructed icons also have a native 48-pixel preview in both themes.

Review scope and evidence

Every icon in the fixed 977-file cohort was examined again with enlarged ink, thin centerlines and native-size previews. The construction audit also reads the segments inside each path: duplicated edges, tiny cubic fragments, curve tangents, straight corners and approximate attachment points. A low stroke count can still hide many fitted curve segments.

The latest repairs include the ten reported examples and defects found throughout the individual review. Each repair replaces geometry in its existing source file. Original source IDs and names are preserved. All published cohort icons pass the full validation checks with no warnings; validation thresholds were unchanged.

Original source snapshots, hashes, comparison sheets and validation results are retained. Panoramic, the game controller, the diagonal pen and the Kubernetes border also retain their specific symmetry and geometry checks. A retained drawing means no further repair was selected after review; it is not a claim that visual quality can be proved by a numeric test.

Construction references include the existing subject silhouettes, local Lucide pencil, dollar-sign, sliders-horizontal, trash-2, git-compare-arrows, brain, signpost and other previously inspected primitives. Shared human reference drawings guide facial simplicity. The original remaining 898 are still available as a filter.
